summary.one_liner: A curated "awesome" list of geospatial and GIS resources, covering desktop and web GIS software, mapping libraries by programming language, spatial databases, datasets, data formats, conferences, news, courses and podcasts.
summary.what_it_does: The README is a link-style list organized into a table of contents with sections such as Geographic Information System Software, Remote Sensing Software, Web Map Servers, Front-end Frameworks, Spatial Databases, and Mobile Develop Tools. The largest part groups geospatial libraries by programming language, from C and C++ through Python, JavaScript, Go, Java, Julia and others. Each entry is one line with a short description, and some entries point to external projects. Other sections cover deep learning for satellite and aerial imagery, open standards, cloud and SaaS services, conferences and communities, MOOCs, podcasts and reference material. The list is inspired by Awesome Python and invites contributions.
use_cases: find open source GIS desktop software
discover geospatial libraries for a programming language
choose a spatial database or map server
find satellite imagery datasets and deep learning tools
locate GIS courses, podcasts and communities
notable: Organized by programming language, with sections for C, C++, Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, Julia and more
Covers both open source and commercial GIS products, marked as such in entries
Includes deep learning frameworks and datasets for remote sensing
Listed in awesome-selfhosted under Maps and GPS, with cross-links to awesome-openstreetmap
caveats: Entries are one-line descriptions with links only in some cases, so the list does not verify whether projects are still maintained
Includes proprietary commercial products such as ArcGIS and ENVI alongside open source tools, so it is not all self-hostable
